intended_object: The relative norm (trace) map N_{U/V}: x ↦ Σ_{t ∈ U/V} t·x from V-invariants to U-invariants, for open normal subgroups V ≤ U of G. It is restricted to the closed coefficient submodules chosen by a RestrictedLevelSystem and bundled as a continuous homomorphism in CompHausAddCommGrp. Inferred from the docstring and the surrounding definitions (`relativeNorm`, `group`, `continuous_relativeNorm`).
explanation: The body bundles the existing restricted relative norm `S.relativeNorm U V h` (as an additive map) with its continuity proof `S.continuous_relativeNorm` into a morphism `S.group V ⟶ S.group U` in CompHausAddCommGrp via `ConcreteCategory.ofHom`. `S.group U` is the chosen closed coefficient submodule with the topology inherited from the LevelCompact topology, so it is compact Hausdorff. The underlying `LevelCompact.relativeNorm` is x ↦ Σ_{t∈T} t⁻¹·x for a right transversal T of V in U, and the library proves it does not depend on T. Summing t⁻¹ over a right transversal runs over the left cosets of V in U, so this is the standard norm map from V-invariants to U-invariants. `S.relativeNorm` restricts it, using the structure field that relative norms preserve the chosen submodules. `relativeNormHom_apply` confirms that the bundled map evaluates as the underlying map. The setting (compact topological group, open normal subgroups, representation over a commutative ring) is the library's own framework for this construction, and the target category is the one the coefficient groups are built in, so the definition is not too narrow. Mathlib has no relative norm between invariants of open subgroups in this bundled topological setting.
